_about: What's new, shown once after an update on the phone and the computer. Newest first; add an entry with every build. platforms: ios, desktop (leave out for both), android (Android shows only notes marked android).

notes.text: Podcasts have their own tab: follow shows and YouTube channels and see their new episodes, with a page for each show.
Find them in Search → Podcasts (Apple's podcast directory and YouTube), or paste a show's feed link, its Apple Podcasts page, or a YouTube link to play any video.
New songs and albums from artists you follow: Drift checks every few hours, even when it's closed, and lets you know. They're also listed under the bell on Home.
Listen Together invites now arrive as notifications too. Choose which you get in Settings → Notifications.
Share a song from its menu: a picture of it (cover, title and artist) for a story or a chat, or a YouTube Music link. You can also copy the link.
Edit playlist (in a playlist's ⋮ menu): rename it, and give it a cover from its songs, a colour with a symbol, or your own photo. You can also choose whether it shows on your profile.
Edit songs: drag songs into a new order, or take them out.
Covers set on your iPhone or computer now show here too.

A song in a playlist or Liked songs plays the wrong version (a live take, a music video)? In its menu, tap Replace with another version and pick the right one from YouTube Music or YouTube. You can listen to each first.
The swap syncs to your iPhone and computer, like the ones made there show up here.
An equalizer with the same 10 bands and presets as the iPhone and computer: Settings → Playback → Equalizer. It works on streamed and downloaded songs, through the speaker, headphones or Bluetooth.
Skips the parts of music videos that aren't music (intros, outros, talking), using SponsorBlock, the same as the iPhone and computer.
When a song ends in a long stretch of silence, Drift moves on to the next one. Both can be turned off in Settings → Playback.
Listening stats: your top songs and artists, and how many minutes you listen, over 4 weeks, 6 months, this year or all time. Tap the chart button on Home, or Settings → Listening stats.
With a Drift profile, it adds up what you play on your iPhone and computer too.
Listen to the same songs at the same time as friends, each on your own device. In the player, tap Together to start a session or join one, with a code or from a friend.
Invite friends from a song's menu: Invite to listen together. Their invites pop up here too, and you can turn them off in Settings → Friends can invite me.
Control your computer from the phone: in the player, tap Devices and pick it. What's playing moves over, and the phone becomes a remote with play, skip, seek and volume.
Your computer and iPhone can control this phone too. Tap Devices → This phone to bring the music back.
Share a playlist with friends: open it, tap ⋮ → Share with friends. Everyone in it can add, remove and reorder songs, and changes show up for all.
Playlists friends share with you appear in Your Library by themselves, including ones shared from an iPhone or computer.
Follow friends and see what they're listening to: tap the people button at the top of Home, and search by name or username.
Friends' profiles show what they're playing and the playlists they share. Play them, or save a copy.
Friends see what you're listening to, and your playlists (all but private ones). Turn sharing off in Settings → Profile & devices.
When a new version is out, Drift says so and installs it with one tap. Your library stays. You can also check in Settings.

When a new version is out, Drift says so and opens SideStore, which installs it with one tap. The first time, SideStore adds Drift's source; after that it also shows updates by itself. Check any time in Settings.
Album covers and playlist pictures no longer take minutes to appear on some networks: they now use the same quick connection as search and playback.
Playlist folders: make one with + in Your Library, and hold a playlist → Move to folder. Folders sync with your other devices.
Follow artists from their page. They show under Artists in Your Library and sync with your other devices.
Bring a Spotify playlist or album into Drift: in Your Library, tap + → Import from Spotify and paste its link. Or share the link from Spotify straight to Drift.
Whole playlists of any length are read, songs you already have are reused, and anything not found is listed, to look for again or copy.
Lyrics in the player: tap Lyrics at the bottom left. Synced lyrics follow the song, and tapping a line jumps there. Songs without synced lyrics show the plain text from Genius.

Download playlists and Liked songs with the arrow next to the play button, or a single song from its menu. Downloaded songs play without internet, and songs added to a downloaded playlist download too.
Recently played songs are kept on the phone (500 MB by default), so they start at once and play offline. Change the size in Settings → Storage.
Downloads wait for Wi-Fi unless you allow mobile data in Settings → Storage.
Playlists and liked songs now sync with your profile: make a playlist here and it shows up in Drift on your linked computer, and the other way round. Deleting a playlist removes it everywhere.
Drift syncs when you open it, a few seconds after you change something, and every couple of minutes while it plays. See the status, or sync by hand, in Settings → Profile & devices.
Unlinking your phone now removes that profile's playlists, liked songs and followed artists from this computer. They stay in your profile and come back when you link it again.
Linking this computer to a different profile than before now replaces its library with that profile's, instead of copying the old profile's playlists into it.
Deleting your profile now also removes its synced library, so a new profile starts empty.
Settings: tap the circle at the top right of Home. From there you can let Drift keep playing in the background, and see What's new again.
Make a Drift profile with a username, a name and a photo, under Settings → Profile & devices. No email or password needed.
Link a computer: type the code Drift shows on your computer to sign it in to your profile. Your library starts syncing in the next update.
Fixed searches timing out on networks where the newer kind of internet address (IPv6) doesn't work. Drift now uses the address that works, as browsers do.
Search no longer loads forever: it now asks YouTube Music directly, the same way Drift on iPhone and computer does. Artist and album pages too.
Songs start faster, with the same quick audio links as on iPhone.
If a search does fail, Drift now says why instead of loading without end.
In a smaller window, the search button in Your Library no longer slides under the main page. When the filters don't all fit, they scroll sideways instead.
The first Android version of Drift: search songs, artists and albums, and play anything from YouTube Music.
Keeps playing with the screen off, with controls on the lock screen, in the notification and on Bluetooth headphones and car stereos.
Queue and shuffle: hold a song for Play next and Add to queue, and tap Queue in the player to move or remove songs.
Playlists and Liked songs in Your Library. Make playlists with +, save albums, and hold a playlist to rename or delete it.
Settings are grouped into Playback, Podcasts, Lyrics, Storage and Look. Tap one to open its page. Your profile and Link a computer are at the top.
Settings are grouped into tabs: Playback, Podcasts, Look, Downloads, Phone & connections, and Computer & updates. Drift remembers the last one you opened.

entries.title: Skip silence is a setting again

notes.text: You can turn skipping dead air at the end of songs on or off again, in Settings → Ad-free listening → Skip silence at the end. It's on by default.

entries.title: No more skips in the middle of downloaded songs

notes.text: Downloaded and cached songs no longer skip parts in the middle. Drift was using the music video's skip times (intros, outros) on the album version it had saved, so they landed in the wrong places.
Songs playing over AirPlay are no longer mistaken for silence.
Drift now looks for updates every hour instead of every 4 hours. A downloaded update installs by itself once nothing has played for 3 minutes, and Drift opens again on the same song.
New in Settings → Computer: when Drift opens at sign-in, it can start minimized to the taskbar instead of opening its window. Turn on Open Drift when you sign in to see it.
Drift no longer mistakes a quiet break or a soft ending for silence, so songs play to the end. Only real dead air (15 seconds or more) is skipped now.
Hold a playlist in Your Library and drag it onto a folder to put it there.
Drag a playlist onto a folder in the sidebar to put it there, or drag it back onto the list to take it out.
Right-click the empty part of the sidebar's playlists to make a new playlist or folder, or import from Spotify (the same as the + button).
The lock screen widget is now a filled circle with the Drift logo cut out, like Spotify's.

The bottom of the player now has three buttons: Devices (AirPlay, Bluetooth and your computer, all in one place), Lyrics and Queue. Listen Together and the stream info moved to the ••• menu, and the top of the player shows when you're listening together.
Fixed songs jumping back to the start a second after they began playing.

entries.title: Equalizer, and play on your other devices

notes.text: Play on another device: tap the speaker button in the player and pick your computer. The music moves there, and this iPhone becomes its remote (play, pause, skip, seek, volume, and anything you pick to play). Tap This iPhone to bring it back. Your computer shows up while Drift is open on it.

Play on another device: click the devices button next to the volume and pick your phone. The music moves there, and this computer becomes its remote (play, pause, skip, seek, volume, and anything you pick to play). Click Play here to bring it back. Your phone shows up while Drift is open or playing on it.
Equalizer: 10 bands and presets like Bass boost, Vocal and Loudness, in Settings › Equalizer. It shapes everything you play on this iPhone (not over AirPlay, where the speaker plays the sound).
Equalizer: 10 bands and presets like Bass boost, Vocal and Loudness, in Settings › Equalizer. It shapes everything you play on this computer.
Songs that end in minutes of silence now move on to the next song by themselves, like on the phone.

entries.title: No more silence at the end of songs

notes.text: Songs that end in minutes of silence now move on to the next song by themselves. This is always on, so the Skip silence setting is gone.
Downloaded and cached songs end right on time, even when iOS thinks the file is longer than the song.

entries.title: Queue, folders, sharing and your listening stats

notes.text: Queue: tap the list button in the player to see what's next. Tap a song to play it, hold and drag to move it, swipe to remove it. Songs also have Add to queue now.
Playlist folders: group playlists in Your Library. Make one with + (New folder), then hold a playlist and pick Move to folder. Folders sync with your computer.
Playlist folders: group playlists in Your Library. Make one with + (New folder), then right-click a playlist and pick Move to folder. Folders sync with your phone.
Share a song: pick Share in a song's menu to send a link, or a picture of the song (cover, title and artist) for a story or a chat.

Listening stats: your minutes, top artists and top songs for the last 4 weeks, 6 months, this year or all time. Open the menu with your profile picture. Songs count from now on, once you've listened for 30 seconds, and your phone and computer add up.

Listening stats: your minutes, top artists and top songs for the last 4 weeks, 6 months, this year or all time. Find it in your profile menu (top right), or in the sidebar in the Apple Music style. Songs count from now on, once you've listened for 30 seconds, and your phone and computer add up.

entries.title: A Drift button for your lock screen

notes.text: Lock screen widget: add Drift's logo to your lock screen and tap it to open the app. Hold the lock screen, tap Customize, then tap the widget area under the clock and pick Drift.

entries.title: Display names, a song cache, and smoother Listen Together

notes.text: Display names: pick the name friends see, with capitals, spaces and emoji. Your @username stays as it is, and people can be found by either.
Display names: pick the name friends see (Edit profile), with capitals, spaces and emoji. Your @username stays as it is, and people can be found by either.
Listen Together invites now pop up right away while Drift is open, even over the player or another screen.
Invites that arrive while Drift plays in the background come as a notification, with Join and Decline right on it.
Invites that arrive while Drift is minimised or in the tray come as a notification.
Listen Together: when a friend's song is still loading, your music no longer jumps back to the start.
Songs you've played are kept on your iPhone (up to 1 GB, change it in Settings), so they start instantly next time and use no data.
Your downloads now show in the Files app (On My iPhone › Drift › Downloads), named by artist and title.
Add to playlist and the other song options now open right away in the full-screen player.
Shared playlists update within a few seconds while you're looking at them (pull down to refresh), and cover changes are shared too.
Shared playlists update within a few seconds while you're looking at them, and cover changes are shared too.
What's new now shows which build each change came with.
What's new now shows which version each change came with.
Tap Followers or Following on any profile to see who's in them.
Tap the version at the bottom of Settings to see what's new again.
Click the version at the bottom of Settings to see what's new again.
Listen Together invites: clearer messages when an invite can't be sent.

entries.title: Listen Together invites, and podcasts from anywhere

notes.text: Invite friends to listen together from any song's ⋯ menu. They get a popup to join or decline.
Only friends who follow each other can invite. You can turn invites off in your profile settings.
Only friends who follow each other can invite. You can turn invites off in Settings.
Podcasts from Apple Podcasts: search a show's name, or paste its Apple Podcasts, SoundCloud or feed link.
YouTube podcasts now list only the episodes on a channel's Podcasts tab, and their whole back catalogue.
Members-only videos are left out of YouTube results.
Podcast episodes can be downloaded.
